verses.zh: 耶和华的话又临到我说：
verses.en: The Lord’s message came to me:

verses.zh: 「人子啊，你要使耶路撒冷知道她那些可憎的事，
verses.en: “Son of man, confront Jerusalem[NOTE:1] with her abominable practices
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 说主耶和华对耶路撒冷如此说：你根本，你出世，是在迦南地；你父亲是亚摩利人，你母亲是赫人。
verses.en: and say, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says to Jerusalem: Your origin and your birth were in the land of the Canaanites; your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite.

verses.zh: 论到你出世的景况，在你初生的日子没有为你断脐带，也没有用水洗你，使你洁净，丝毫没有撒盐在你身上，也没有用布裹你。
verses.en: As for your birth, on the day you were born your umbilical cord was not cut, nor were you washed in water;[NOTE:1] you were certainly not rubbed down with salt, nor wrapped with blankets.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “in water you were not washed for cleansing” or “with water you were not washed smooth” (see D. I. Block, Ezekiel [NICOT], 1:473, n. 57, for a discussion of possible meanings of this hapax legomenon).
Arab midwives still cut the umbilical cords of infants and then proceed to apply salt and oil to their bodies.

verses.zh: 谁的眼也不可怜你，为你做一件这样的事怜恤你；但你初生的日子扔在田野，是因你被厌恶。
verses.en: No eye took pity on you to do even one of these things for you to spare you;[NOTE:1] you were thrown out into the open field[NOTE:2] because you were detested on the day you were born.
notes: These verbs, “pity” and “spare,” echo the judgment oracles in 5:11; 7:4, 9; 8:18; 9:5, 10.
A similar concept is found in Deut 32:10.

verses.zh: 「我从你旁边经过，见你滚在血中，就对你说：你虽在血中，仍可存活；你虽在血中，仍可存活。
verses.en: “‘I passed by you and saw you kicking around helplessly in your blood. I said to you as you lay there in your blood, “Live!” I said to you as you lay there in your blood, “Live!”[NOTE:1]
notes: The translation reflects the Hebrew text, which repeats the statement, perhaps for emphasis. However, a few medieval Hebrew manuscripts, the Old Greek, and the Syriac do not include the repetition. The statement could have been accidentally repeated, or the second occurrence could have been accidentally omitted. Based on the available evidence it is difficult to know which is more likely.

verses.zh: 我使你生长好像田间所长的，你就渐渐长大，以致极其俊美，两乳成形，头发长成，你却仍然赤身露体。
verses.en: I made you plentiful like sprouts in a field; you grew tall and came of age so that you could wear jewelry. Your breasts had formed and your hair had grown, but you were still naked and bare.

verses.zh: 我从你旁边经过，看见你的时候正动爱情，便用衣襟搭在你身上，遮盖你的赤体；又向你起誓，与你结盟，你就归于我。这是主耶和华说的。
verses.en: “‘Then I passed by you and watched you, noticing[NOTE:1] that you had reached the age for love.[NOTE:2] I spread my cloak[NOTE:3] over you and covered your nakedness. I swore a solemn oath to you and entered into a marriage covenant with you, declares the Sovereign Lord, and you became mine.
notes: The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a participle.
See similar use of this term in Ezek 23:17; Prov 7:16; Song of Songs 4:10; 7:13.
Heb “wing” or “skirt.” The gesture symbolized acquiring a woman in early Arabia (similarly, see Deut 22:30; Ruth 3:9).

verses.zh: 那时我用水洗你，洗净你身上的血，又用油抹你。
verses.en: “‘Then I bathed you in water, washed the blood off you, and anointed you with fragrant oil.

verses.zh: 我也使你身穿绣花衣服，脚穿海狗皮鞋，并用细麻布给你束腰，用丝绸为衣披在你身上，
verses.en: I dressed you in embroidered clothing and put fine leather sandals on your feet. I wrapped you with fine linen and covered you with silk.

verses.zh: 又用妆饰打扮你，将镯子戴在你手上，将金链戴在你项上。
verses.en: I adorned you with jewelry. I put bracelets on your hands and a necklace around your neck.

verses.zh: 我也将环子戴在你鼻子上，将耳环戴在你耳朵上，将华冠戴在你头上。
verses.en: I put a ring in your nose, earrings on your ears, and a beautiful crown on your head.

verses.zh: 这样，你就有金银的妆饰，穿的是细麻衣和丝绸，并绣花衣；吃的是细面、蜂蜜，并油。你也极其美貌，发达到王后的尊荣。
verses.en: You were adorned with gold and silver, while your clothing was of fine linen, silk, and embroidery. You ate the finest flour, honey, and olive oil. You became extremely beautiful and attained the position of royalty.

verses.zh: 你美貌的名声传在列邦中，你十分美貌，是因我加在你身上的威荣。这是主耶和华说的。
verses.en: Your fame[NOTE:1] spread among the nations because of your beauty; your beauty was perfect because of the splendor that I bestowed on you, declares the Sovereign Lord.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “name.”
The description of the nation Israel in vv. 10-14 recalls the splendor of the nation’s golden age under King Solomon.

verses.zh: 只是你仗着自己的美貌，又因你的名声就行邪淫。你纵情淫乱，使过路的任意而行。
verses.en: “‘But you trusted in your beauty and capitalized on your fame by becoming a prostitute. You offered your sexual favors to every man who passed by so that your beauty[NOTE:1] became his.
notes: Heb “it” (so KJV, ASV); the referent (the beauty in which the prostitute trusted; see the beginning of the verse) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 你用衣服为自己在高处结彩，在其上行邪淫。这样的事将来必没有，也必不再行了。
verses.en: You took some of your clothing and made for yourself decorated high places; you engaged in prostitution on them. You went to him to become his.[NOTE:1]
notes: The text as written in the MT is incomprehensible (“not coming [plural] and he will not”). Driver has suggested a copying error of similar-sounding words, specifically לֹא (loʾ) for לוֹ (lo). The feminine participle בָאוֹת (vaʾot) has also been read as the feminine perfect בָאת (vaʾt). See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 1:228, n. 15.b, and D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:486, n. 137.

verses.zh: 你又将我所给你那华美的金银、宝器为自己制造人像，与他行邪淫；
verses.en: You also took your beautiful jewelry, made of my gold and my silver I had given to you, and made for yourself male images and engaged in prostitution[NOTE:1] with them.
notes: Or perhaps “and worshiped them,” if the word “prostitution” is understood in a figurative rather than a literal sense (cf. CEV, NLT).

verses.zh: 又用你的绣花衣服给他披上，并将我的膏油和香料摆在他跟前；
verses.en: You took your embroidered clothing and used it to cover them; you offered my olive oil and my incense to them.

verses.zh: 又将我赐给你的食物，就是我赐给你吃的细面、油，和蜂蜜，都摆在他跟前为馨香的供物。这是主耶和华说的。
verses.en: As for my food that I gave you—the fine flour, olive oil, and honey I fed you—you placed it before them as a soothing aroma. That is exactly what happened, declares the Sovereign Lord.

verses.zh: 并且你将给我所生的儿女焚献给他。
verses.en: “‘You took your sons and your daughters whom you bore to me and you sacrificed them[NOTE:1] as food for the idols to eat. As if your prostitution was not enough,
notes: The sacrifice of children was prohibited in Lev 18:21; 20:2; Deut 12:31; 18:10.

verses.zh: 你行淫乱岂是小事，竟将我的儿女杀了，使他们经火归与他吗？
verses.en: you slaughtered my children and sacrificed them to the idols.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and you gave them, by passing them through to them.” Some believe this alludes to the pagan practice of making children pass through the fire.

verses.zh: 你行这一切可憎和淫乱的事，并未追念你幼年赤身露体滚在血中的日子。
verses.en: And with all your abominable practices and prostitution you did not remember the days of your youth when you were naked and bare, kicking around in your blood.

verses.zh: 你行这一切恶事之后（主耶和华说：你有祸了！有祸了！）
verses.en: “‘After all your evil—“Woe! Woe to you!” declares the Sovereign Lord—

verses.zh: 又为自己建造圆顶花楼，在各街上做了高台。
verses.en: you built yourself a chamber[NOTE:1] and put up a pavilion[NOTE:2] in every public square.
notes: The Hebrew גֶּב (gev) may represent more than one word, each rare in the Old Testament. It may refer to a “mound” or to “rafters.” The LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate interpret this as a brothel.
Or “lofty place” (NRSV). See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 1:229, and B. Lang, Frau Weisheit, 137.

verses.zh: 你在一切市口上建造高台，使你的美貌变为可憎的，又与一切过路的多行淫乱。
verses.en: At the head of every street you erected your pavilion, and you disgraced[NOTE:1] your beauty when you spread[NOTE:2] your legs to every passerby and multiplied your promiscuity.
notes: Heb “treated as if abominable,” i.e., repudiated.
The only other occurrence of the Hebrew root is found in Prov 13:3 in reference to the talkative person who habitually “opens wide” his lips.

verses.zh: 你也和你邻邦放纵情欲的埃及人行淫，加增你的淫乱，惹我发怒。
verses.en: You engaged in prostitution with the Egyptians, your lustful neighbors,[NOTE:1] multiplying your promiscuity and provoking me to anger.
notes: Heb “your neighbors, large of flesh.” The word “flesh” is used here of the genitals. It may simply refer to the size of their genitals in general, or that they are lustful.

verses.zh: 因此我伸手攻击你，减少你应用的粮食，又将你交给恨你的非利士众女（众女是城邑的意思；本章下同），使她们任意待你。她们见你的淫行，为你羞耻。
verses.en: So see here, I have stretched out my hand against you and cut off your rations. I have delivered you into the power of those who hate you, the daughters of the Philistines, who were ashamed of your obscene conduct.

verses.zh: 你因贪色无厌，又与亚述人行淫，与他们行淫之后，仍不满意，
verses.en: You engaged in prostitution with the Assyrians because your desires were insatiable; you prostituted yourself with them and yet you were still not satisfied.

verses.zh: 并且多行淫乱，直到那贸易之地，就是迦勒底，你仍不满意。
verses.en: Then you multiplied your promiscuity to the land of merchants, Babylonia,[NOTE:1] but you were not satisfied there either.
notes: Heb “Chaldea.” The name of the tribal group ruling Babylon (“Chaldeans”) and the territory from which they originated (“Chaldea”) are used as metonymy for the whole empire of Babylon.

verses.zh: 主耶和华说：你行这一切事，都是不知羞耻妓女所行的，可见你的心是何等懦弱！
verses.en: “‘How sick is your heart, declares the Sovereign Lord, when you perform all these acts, the deeds of a bold prostitute.

verses.zh: 因你在一切市口上建造圆顶花楼，在各街上做了高台，你却藐视赏赐，不像妓女。
verses.en: When you built your chamber at the head of every street and put up your pavilion in every public square, you were not like a prostitute, because you scoffed at payment.[NOTE:1]
notes: The Hebrew term, which also occurs in vv. 34 and 41 of this chapter, always refers to the payment of a prostitute (Deut 23:19; Isa 23:17; Hos 9:1; Mic 1:7).

verses.zh: 哎！你这行淫的妻啊，宁肯接外人，不接丈夫。
verses.en: “‘Adulterous wife, who prefers strangers instead of her own husband!

verses.zh: 凡妓女是得人赠送，你反倒赠送你所爱的人，贿赂他们从四围来与你行淫。
verses.en: All prostitutes receive payment,[NOTE:1] but instead you give gifts to every one of your lovers. You bribe them to come to you from all around for your sexual favors!
notes: The Hebrew word occurs only here in the OT.

verses.zh: 你行淫与别的妇女相反，因为不是人从你行淫；你既赠送人，人并不赠送你；所以你与别的妇女相反。
verses.en: You were different from other prostitutes[NOTE:1] because no one solicited you. When you gave payment and no payment was given to you, you became the opposite!
notes: Heb “With you it was opposite of women in your prostitution.”

verses.zh: 你这妓女啊，要听耶和华的话。
verses.en: “‘Therefore, you prostitute, listen to the Lord’s message!

verses.zh: 主耶和华如此说：因你的污秽倾泄了，你与你所爱的行淫露出下体，又因你拜一切可憎的偶像，流儿女的血献给他，
verses.en: This is what the Sovereign Lord says: Because your lust[NOTE:1] was poured out and your nakedness was uncovered in your prostitution with your lovers, and because of all your detestable idols, and because of the blood of your children you have given to them,
notes: The Hebrew word occurs only here in the OT.

verses.zh: 我就要将你一切相欢、相爱的，和你一切所恨的都聚集来，从四围攻击你；又将你的下体露出，使他们看尽了。
verses.en: therefore, take note: I am about to gather all your lovers whom you enjoyed, both all those you loved and all those you hated. I will gather them against you from all around, and I will expose your nakedness to them, and they will see all your nakedness.[NOTE:1]
notes: Harlots suffered degradation when their nakedness was exposed (Jer 13:22, 26; Hos 2:12; Nah 3:5).

verses.zh: 我也要审判你，好像官长审判淫妇和流人血的妇女一样。我因忿怒忌恨，使流血的罪归到你身上。
verses.en: I will punish you as an adulteress and murderer deserves.[NOTE:1] I will avenge your bloody deeds with furious rage.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and I will judge you (with) the judgments of adulteresses and of those who shed blood.”
Heb “and I will give you the blood of rage and zeal.”

verses.zh: 我又要将你交在他们手中；他们必拆毁你的圆顶花楼，毁坏你的高台，剥去你的衣服，夺取你的华美宝器，留下你赤身露体。
verses.en: I will give you into their hands, and they will destroy your chambers and tear down your pavilions. They will strip you of your clothing and take your beautiful jewelry and leave you naked and bare.

verses.zh: 他们也必带多人来攻击你，用石头打死你，用刀剑刺透你，
verses.en: They will summon a mob who will stone you and hack you in pieces with their swords.

verses.zh: 用火焚烧你的房屋，在许多妇人眼前向你施行审判。我必使你不再行淫，也不再赠送与人。
verses.en: They will burn down your houses and execute judgments on you in front of many women. Thus I will put a stop to your prostitution, and you will no longer give gifts to your clients.[NOTE:1]
notes: The words “to your clients” are not in the Hebrew text but are implied.

verses.zh: 这样，我就止息向你发的忿怒，我的忌恨也要离开你，我要安静不再恼怒。
verses.en: I will exhaust my rage on you, and then my fury will turn from you. I will calm down and no longer be angry.

verses.zh: 因你不追念你幼年的日子，在这一切的事上向我发烈怒，所以我必照你所行的报应在你头上，你就不再贪淫，行那一切可憎的事。这是主耶和华说的。
verses.en: “‘Because you did not remember the days of your youth and have enraged me with all these deeds, I hereby repay you for what you have done,[NOTE:1] declares the Sovereign Lord. Have you not engaged in prostitution on top of all your other abominable practices?
notes: Heb “your way on (your) head I have placed.”

verses.zh: 「凡说俗语的必用俗语攻击你，说：『母亲怎样，女儿也怎样。』
verses.en: “‘Observe—everyone who quotes proverbs will quote this proverb about you: “Like mother, like daughter.”

verses.zh: 你正是你母亲的女儿，厌弃丈夫和儿女；你正是你姊妹的姊妹，厌弃丈夫和儿女。你母亲是赫人，你父亲是亚摩利人。
verses.en: You are the daughter of your mother, who detested her husband and her sons, and you are the sister of your sisters, who detested their husbands and their sons. Your mother was a Hittite and your father an Amorite.

verses.zh: 你的姊姊是撒马利亚，她和她的众女住在你左边；你的妹妹是所多玛，她和她的众女住在你右边。
verses.en: Your older sister was Samaria, who lived north[NOTE:1] of you with her daughters, and your younger sister, who lived south[NOTE:2] of you, was Sodom[NOTE:3] with her daughters.
notes: Heb “left.”
Heb “right.”
Sodom was the epitome of evil (Deut 29:23; 32:32; Isa 1:9-10; 3:9; Jer 23:14; Lam 4:6; Matt 10:15; 11:23-24; Jude 7).

verses.zh: 你没有效法她们的行为，也没有照她们可憎的事去做，你以那为小事，你一切所行的倒比她们更坏。
verses.en: Have you not copied their behavior[NOTE:1] and practiced their abominable deeds? In a short time[NOTE:2] you became even more depraved in all your conduct than they were!
notes: Heb “walked in their ways.”
The Hebrew expression has a temporal meaning as illustrated by the use of the phrase in 2 Chr 12:7.

verses.zh: 主耶和华说：我指着我的永生起誓，你妹妹所多玛与她的众女尚未行你和你众女所行的事。
verses.en: As surely as I live, declares the Sovereign Lord, your sister Sodom and her daughters never behaved as wickedly as you and your daughters have behaved.

verses.zh: 看哪，你妹妹所多玛的罪孽是这样：她和她的众女都心骄气傲，粮食饱足，大享安逸，并没有扶助困苦和穷乏人的手。
verses.en: “‘See here—this was the iniquity[NOTE:1] of your sister Sodom: She and her daughters had majesty, abundance of food, and enjoyed carefree ease, but they did not help[NOTE:2] the poor and needy.
notes: Or “guilt.”
Heb “strengthen the hand of.”

verses.zh: 她们狂傲，在我面前行可憎的事，我看见便将她们除掉。
verses.en: They were haughty and practiced abominable deeds before me. Therefore, when I saw it I removed them.

verses.zh: 撒马利亚没有犯你一半的罪，你行可憎的事比她更多，使你的姊妹因你所行一切可憎的事，倒显为义。
verses.en: Samaria has not committed half the sins you have; you have done more abominable deeds than they did.[NOTE:1] You have made your sisters appear righteous with all the abominable things you have done.
notes: Or “you have multiplied your abominable deeds beyond them.”

verses.zh: 你既断定你姊妹为义（为义：或译当受羞辱），就要担当自己的羞辱；因你所犯的罪比她们更为可憎，她们就比你更显为义；你既使你的姊妹显为义，你就要抱愧担当自己的羞辱。」
verses.en: So now, bear your disgrace, because you have given your sisters reason to justify their behavior.[NOTE:1] Because the sins you have committed were more abominable than those of your sisters; they have become more righteous than you. So now, be ashamed and bear the disgrace of making your sisters appear righteous.
notes: Heb “because you have interceded for your sisters with your sins.”

verses.zh: 「我必叫她们被掳的归回，就是叫所多玛和她的众女，撒马利亚和她的众女，并你们中间被掳的，都要归回，
verses.en: “‘I will restore their fortunes, the fortunes of Sodom and her daughters, and the fortunes of Samaria and her daughters (along with your fortunes among them),

verses.zh: 好使你担当自己的羞辱，并因你一切所行的使她们得安慰，你就抱愧。
verses.en: so that you may bear your disgrace and be ashamed of all you have done in consoling them.

verses.zh: 你的妹妹所多玛和她的众女必归回原位；撒马利亚和她的众女，你和你的众女，也必归回原位。
verses.en: As for your sisters, Sodom and her daughters will be restored to their former status, Samaria and her daughters will be restored to their former status, and you and your daughters will be restored to your former status.

verses.zh: 在你骄傲的日子，你的恶行没有显露以先，你的口就不提你的妹妹所多玛。那受了凌辱的亚兰众女和亚兰四围非利士的众女都恨恶你，藐视你。
verses.en: In your days of majesty,[NOTE:1] was not Sodom your sister a byword in your mouth,
notes: Or “pride.”

verses.zh: a
verses.en: before your evil was exposed? Now you have become an object of scorn to the daughters of Aram[NOTE:1] and all those around her and to the daughters of the Philistines—those all around you who despise you.
notes: So MT, LXX, and Vulgate; many Hebrew mss and the Syriac read “Edom.”

verses.zh: 耶和华说：你贪淫和可憎的事，你已经担当了。」
verses.en: You must bear your punishment for your obscene conduct and your abominable practices, declares the Lord.

verses.zh: 「主耶和华如此说：你这轻看誓言、背弃盟约的，我必照你所行的待你。
verses.en: “‘For this is what the Sovereign Lord says: I will deal with you according to what you have done when you despised your oath by breaking your covenant.

verses.zh: 然而我要追念在你幼年时与你所立的约，也要与你立定永约。
verses.en: Yet I will remember the covenant I made with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish a lasting[NOTE:1] covenant with you.
notes: Or “eternal.”

verses.zh: 你接待你姊姊和你妹妹的时候，你要追念你所行的，自觉惭愧；并且我要将她们赐你为女儿，却不是按着前约。
verses.en: Then you will remember your conduct and be ashamed when you receive your older and younger sisters. I will give them to you as daughters, but not on account of my covenant with you.

verses.zh: 我要坚定与你所立的约（你就知道我是耶和华），
verses.en: I will establish my covenant with you, and then you will know that I am the Lord.

verses.zh: 好使你在我赦免你一切所行的时候，心里追念，自觉抱愧，又因你的羞辱就不再开口。这是主耶和华说的。」
verses.en: Then you will remember, be ashamed, and remain silent[NOTE:1] because of your disgrace when I make atonement for all you have done,[NOTE:2] declares the Sovereign Lord.’”
notes: Heb “and your mouth will not be open any longer.”
Heb “when I make atonement for you for all that you have done.”
